questions.yaml:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schema/question.schema.json
slug: streamwriter-not-flushed-memorystream-empty
stack: dotnet
topic: clr-gc
level: middle
type: find-bug
grading: auto
tags: [idisposable, streamwriter, buffering, using]
code:
  language: csharp
  harness: statements
  source: |
    MemoryStream stream = new MemoryStream();
    StreamWriter writer = new StreamWriter(stream);
    writer.Write("Hello");
    Console.WriteLine(stream.Length);
bugLineSets: [[2]]
fixedSource: |
  using MemoryStream stream = new MemoryStream();
  using (StreamWriter writer = new StreamWriter(stream, leaveOpen: true))
  {
      writer.Write("Hello");
  }
  Console.WriteLine(stream.Length);
fixedExpect: { kind: output, value: "5" }
links:
  - url: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.streamwriter.autoflush
    lang: en
    kind: docs
  - url: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/garbage-collection/using-objects
    lang: en
    kind: docs
locales:
  ru:
    title: Почему MemoryStream пуст после записи через StreamWriter?
    prompt: |
      Программа пишет строку `"Hello"` в `MemoryStream` через `StreamWriter` и должна вывести длину потока `5`,
      но выводит `0`. Исключений нет. Щёлкните по строке с дефектом.
    hint: Куда на самом деле попадают символы после `writer.Write`, и кто отвечает за то, чтобы они дошли до потока?
    answer: Строка 2, `StreamWriter` создаётся без блока `using`, поэтому его никто не сбрасывает и не освобождает до чтения `stream.Length`.
    explanation: |
      `StreamWriter` буферизует вывод: `Write` складывает символы во внутренний буфер, а в нижележащий поток
      байты попадают только при `Flush`, `Dispose` (или `Close`) либо когда буфер заполнится. Свойство
      `AutoFlush` по умолчанию равно `false`, поэтому после `writer.Write("Hello")` в `MemoryStream` ещё ничего
      нет, и `stream.Length` равно `0`.

      Дефект в строке 2: писатель - это `IDisposable`, но он создан без `using`, и до чтения длины его никто не
      сбрасывает. Сборщик мусора здесь не поможет: он не вызывает `Dispose`, а данные из буфера, который так и
      не сбросили, просто теряются.

      Исправление - ограничить время жизни писателя блоком `using`, который закрывается до чтения `Length`.
      Две детали:

      - объявление `using StreamWriter writer = ...;` без фигурных скобок здесь не подходит: `Dispose` вызовется
        в конце области видимости, то есть уже после `Console.WriteLine`, и программа снова выведет `0`;
      - по умолчанию `Dispose` у `StreamWriter` закрывает и сам поток, а чтение `Length` у закрытого
        `MemoryStream` выбрасывает `ObjectDisposedException`. Поэтому в исправлении передан `leaveOpen: true`.

      Другой вариант - вызвать `writer.Flush()` перед чтением длины. В .NET 10 кодировка `StreamWriter` по
      умолчанию - UTF-8 без BOM, поэтому пять ASCII-символов дают ровно 5 байт.
    linkTitles:
      - "Свойство StreamWriter.AutoFlush"
      - "Использование объектов, реализующих IDisposable"
  en:
    title: Why is a MemoryStream empty after writing to it through a StreamWriter?
    prompt: |
      The program writes the string `"Hello"` to a `MemoryStream` through a `StreamWriter` and should print the
      stream length `5`, but it prints `0`. No exception is thrown. Click the line that contains the defect.
    hint: Where do the characters actually go after `writer.Write`, and who is responsible for getting them to the stream?
    answer: Line 2, the `StreamWriter` is created without a `using` block, so nothing flushes or disposes it before `stream.Length` is read.
    explanation: |
      `StreamWriter` buffers its output: `Write` puts the characters into an internal buffer, and bytes reach the
      underlying stream only on `Flush`, `Dispose` (or `Close`), or when the buffer fills up. `AutoFlush` is
      `false` by default, so after `writer.Write("Hello")` the `MemoryStream` is still empty and `stream.Length`
      is `0`.

      The defect is on line 2: the writer is an `IDisposable`, but it is created without `using`, and nothing
      flushes it before the length is read. The garbage collector does not help here: it does not call `Dispose`,
      and data left in a buffer that was never flushed is simply lost.

      The fix is to limit the writer's lifetime with a `using` block that closes before `Length` is read.
      Two details:

      - a `using StreamWriter writer = ...;` declaration without braces does not work here: `Dispose` runs at the
        end of the scope, which is after `Console.WriteLine`, so the program would print `0` again;
      - by default `Dispose` on a `StreamWriter` also closes the stream, and reading `Length` of a closed
        `MemoryStream` throws `ObjectDisposedException`. That is why the fix passes `leaveOpen: true`.

      Another option is to call `writer.Flush()` before reading the length. On .NET 10 the default encoding of
      `StreamWriter` is UTF-8 without a BOM, so five ASCII characters give exactly 5 bytes.
    linkTitles:
      - "StreamWriter.AutoFlush property"
      - "Using objects that implement IDisposable"
meta:

notes.text: The defect is a missing statement, so the clickable line is debatable. Only line 2 (writer created without using) is accepted. A reader might argue for line 4 (reading Length before a flush). Consider adding [4] as a second accepted set if review prefers that.

The fixed code relies on the constructor StreamWriter(Stream stream, Encoding? encoding = null, int bufferSize = -1, bool leaveOpen = false) and is called with the named argument leaveOpen: true. I believe these optional parameters have existed since .NET Core 3.0. Confirm by running run-snippets.

Expected buggy output 0 assumes that StreamWriter.Write(string) does not touch the stream until a flush, and that the default UTF8 encoding (no BOM) writes no preamble. Expected fixed output 5 assumes the same no-BOM default. Verify both in the sandbox.

The explanation claims that MemoryStream.Length on a closed stream throws ObjectDisposedException. It also implies that StreamWriter has no finalizer that flushes the buffer, so unflushed data is lost. I am fairly but not fully certain of both.
